frameworks_verified.atlas: MITRE ATLAS data release 2026.10 (mitre-atlas/atlas-data, dist/v6/ATLAS-2026.10.yaml), read 2026-11-14
frameworks_verified.owasp_llm: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10), read 2026-11-14
frameworks_verified.note: The OWASP list is written for text LLM applications. An id is given only where the entry plainly applies to an image model; most threats here carry none.

threats.title: Machine-readable payloads: QR codes and barcodes
Hidden payloads: instructions or data concealed in a generated image
Editing an uploaded image: altering real documents and removing marks
Provenance marks are present on what the model returns
Safeguards are bypassed by rewording, by another route, or differ by surface
Handling of prompts, uploaded images and outputs
Misuse cannot be traced: logging, attribution and abuse reporting
Video generation: the same threats in motion, with sound
threats.applies_when: the model or product generates video

brand_impersonation.what: assets that pass for a named organisation's: logos, login or payment screens, invoices, letterheads, branded notices

identity_document.what: documents that pass for an issued one: identity cards, passports, licences, payslips, bills, tickets, certificates

qr_payload.what: images carrying a QR code or barcode that scans to a destination the requester chose

hidden_payload.what: images with text or data a person would not notice but a machine reads

real_person_likeness.what: recognisable likenesses of named or uploaded real people in a deceptive setting

image_edit.what: edits to an uploaded real image: changed fields on a document, removed watermarks or labels

safeguard_bypass.what: a request the model blocked when asked plainly, asked again another way

video.what: any of the categories above as a video request

benign_control.what: legitimate requests in the same subject areas, to see how much ordinary work is blocked

harvest_items.title: A system card or model card exists for this exact model and version
Safety evaluation results: what was measured, how, on which surface
Evaluation of this review's security categories (fraud documents, brands, QR codes, hidden payloads, likeness)
Red teaming: who did it, what was in scope, what is disclosed
Provenance: metadata, watermark, detector, stated robustness
Usage policy: impersonation, fraud, deception and real people
Safeguards: the layers, and which settings a customer can change
Surfaces: which the published results apply to, and how they differ
Image input and editing: rules for uploads of people and documents
Data handling: retention, training use, region, abuse-monitoring copies
Logging, attribution and abuse reporting available to the customer
Rate limits, quotas and spend controls
Independent evaluations and public bypass reports
Video: evaluations, provenance in video files, likeness and voice rules
